issues.explanation: The candidate id list and the fairness decision at :86 are fixed before the lock/re-check loop, so if concurrent Ticket::call() claims all waiting normals the action throws NoWaitingTicketsException even though priority tickets are waiting, contrary to rule 5 ("priority tickets keep being called").

The race test intercepts any tickets query whose bindings contain the top id; when the queue id equals that ticket id it fires on the fairness query instead of the candidate lock, so the re-check/skip path at app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:42-50 is not reliably exercised, and the DB::beforeExecuting callback is left registered for later tests.
The three-field transition is duplicated instead of reusing the existing Ticket::call() primitive, which risks drifting from any invariants, events or future changes implemented there.
Plucking all candidate ids up front materializes every waiting id before locking; iterating with a cursor/chunk would keep memory flat for large queues.

candidateQuery both builds a query and performs a fairness history read, hiding I/O in a method named like a pure query builder; extracting the fairness decision would make the selection flow easier to follow.

review.summary: The change implements CallNextTicket with the CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException, covering ordering, the three modes, fairness, active-queue validation, exactly-once locking, docs and extensive tests. The core requirements are met, but fairness is not re-evaluated after a concurrent skip and the race test can bypass that path, so this is an approve-with-nits PR rather than a clean pass.
